docs.title: Welcome to Unciv!
docs.text: Unciv is an open source, mod-friendly Android and Desktop remake of Civ V, made with LibGDX. Build your civilization, research technologies, expand your cities and defeat your foes!

docs.title: How do I play?
docs.text:
Unmodded gameplay is equal to Civ V, so any Civ V guide will suffice

The game contains a tutorial to get you started

docs.title: How can I contribute?
docs.text:
The most valuable first step to getting involved is engaging with our community: join the Discord! It's a great place to meet your fellow contributors.

In addition, you can keep track of requests, bugs, and our todo list for the application at the repository's Issue Tracker

If you're a developer, you'll probably want to start at the Getting Started page!

If you're a translator, head over to Translating!

If you're a modder, start here.

If not, you can still help by spreading the word - vote for Unciv where you can, mention it on Reddit or Twitter etc, and help us with new ideas of how to get the word out!

docs.title: The AI plays to win
docs.text:
In a perfect world, the AI would pass the "Turing test" of gameplay - you would't be able to tell if you're playing against a human or AI.

Examples:

  • No "what would you offer me for this"
  • AI will choose to attack you if your military is weak (WILL kick you when you're down)

There is a fine line here between "exploitable" and "no fun" regarding trade - regular players may refuse any trade you offer them on principle. We don't want that from the AI, which leaves us slightly open to exploits, but that's a trade-off we make knowingly.

docs.title: Modding philosophy - minimal objects, maximum interactions
docs.text:
As a new modder it's easy to get lost in the sheer number of uniques.

Our aim is to minimize the number of uniques as much as possible, but enable "emergent modding" by allowing combinations.

Examples:

  • Parameters in uniques > multiple uniques
  • Conditions should be Conditionals, so they can be applied to all uniques
  • Triggered uniques and unique triggers - all combinations
  • Unit Action modifiers, rather than special attributes for specific unit actions

docs.title: Crash early, crash often
docs.text:
A crash stacktrace is halfway to a solution - a game save which reliably produces it is 90% there.

Whenever an unexpected situation occurs - the game has reached an incorrect state - we should crash, to allow the problem to be fixed as soon as possible. Persisting with an incorrect state makes the eventual resulting problems further from the cause, and complicates debugging.

Howver, we should never crash due to bad user input. Bad input - e.g. badly defined mods - are expected, and should be handled accordingly.

This is analogous to the difference between an http 4XX and 5XX - bad inputs are expected at the interface with the world, bad interval state is unexpected.

The goal in both cases is to minimize crashes, only the methodology differs.

docs.title: Authoritative multiplayer command coverage
docs.text: This is the completion ledger for API-v3 gameplay authority. It is based on current source call sites, not intended behavior. A row is Complete only when the public command is closed and versioned, the Kotlin worker calls shared domain logic, Rust derives the actor from session and membership, legality and authorization tests pass, the player projection contains the data needed to issue and reconcile the command, and every online UI call site uses the v3 command bus. A server handler without migrated client call sites is Partial.

docs.title: Current authority boundary
docs.text:
Explicit legacy/API-v2 online play remains client-authored: WorldScreen.nextTurn() clones and advances GameInfo, then calls Multiplayer.updateGame(); Multiplayer.kt also mutates resignation/turn state locally; and MultiplayerServer.uploadGame() sends the resulting whole save. Current API-v3 creation, discovery, world, end-turn, and resignation routes never enter those paths. Historical legacy-shaped v3 interceptors are still being removed or classified by the source-level boundary audit.

API v3 now exposes a closed command union spanning movement, combat, unit orders/actions, city production/economy/population/governance, research, policies, religion, trades, diplomacy, city-state interactions, espionage, voting, great-person choices, and end turn. The production Multiplayer owner installs one AuthoritativeMultiplayerSession, which negotiates capabilities, restores or creates an authenticated session, opens per-game command buses from an HTTP projection, reconciles WebSocket hints through HTTP, and pages through the authenticated account's server-owned game memberships. For an explicitly opened v3 game, WorldScreen.nextTurn() submits through that lifecycle before cloning or advancing local state and never uploads the result. Rows below remain partial or missing where current call sites or required projection data are not yet migrated. API-v3 game creation, discovery, and projection reads are implemented outside the gameplay command union.

Status meanings:

  • Partial: some authoritative protocol/worker/server/test support exists, but required commands, projection data, or client migration remains.
  • Missing: no v3 gameplay command and no authoritative handler exist.
  • Not applicable: local-only presentation behavior that must remain local.

docs.title: Coverage matrix
docs.text: Mutation family Required typed command(s) Shared handler / current mutator Server authorization and validation required Projection and reconciliation effects Current online call sites / evidence Status Server game creation CreateGame resource creation (never a state-upload command); the backend accepts a caller-stable operation ID, pinned manifest hash, and one closed bounded generated-game setup, then generates an independent OS-backed secret map seed inside the control plane GameStarter.startNewGame through HeadlessGameEngine.createGame; the private worker independently validates ruleset-derived choices and materializes GameSetupInfo from the typed setup, pinned manifest, authenticated owner, and server seed Authenticated owner; durable operation identity is bound to the account and canonical manifest/setup meaning; concurrent duplicates serialize and return one game, while changed reuse fails closed; server-approved engine/ruleset manifest; bounded fixed civilization counts, map enum choices, toggles and timers; difficulty/speed/era/victories must exist in the pinned ruleset; no client seed, clock, arbitrary/custom map, setup JSON, GameInfo, snapshot, actor, or revision-zero result; the seed is not derivable from the public game UUID Initial player projection, membership, revision 0, and creation-operation record commit atomically; failed creation leaves neither; the authenticated session requires the operation ID, resolves one exact manifest, creates, fetches the projection, and opens the command bus Production NewGameScreen routes authenticated v3 setup through the server, preserves one operation ID for unchanged meaning, rejects unsupported custom/client-authored choices, validates owner membership/revision/hash/civilization against the returned projection, and opens the projection-only world. Explicit legacy servers cannot create new online games Complete for bounded generated-game production creation and projection-world entry Join and civilization assignment Owner-created durable player invitation plus closed JoinGame HeadlessGameEngine.assignPlayer Enabled target account discovers only its own pending invitations; invitation is required before worker execution and rechecked under the final game lock; server selects an unclaimed civilization; one account/civilization; join uses the actual current revision rather than a revision-zero special case Invitation consumption, membership/civilization, canonical snapshot, revision, journal, and outbox commit atomically; subsequent invited players can join later revisions The production account inbox uses retry-stable acceptance, rediscovers the committed membership, validates the server-assigned civilization and revision/hash, opens the player projection, and transitions directly into the projection-only world. No client civilization or player ID is submitted Complete Unit movement MoveUnit(unitId, destination, escortUnitId?) implements exact current-turn single or atomic escort-pair movement, MoveUnitToward(unitId, finalDestination, escortUnitId?) implements canonical single or paired multi-turn orders, CancelUnitMovementOrder(unitId) cancels an existing canonical route through either pair member, and SwapUnits(unitId, destination) implements compatible friendly occupancy Shared UnitMovement.moveToTile, transient in-worker escort reconstruction, headTowards, serialized MapUnit.action plus stable nullable movementEscortUnitId processing/clearing, and swapMoveToTile(..., keepEscorting = true) through focused movement modules and HeadlessGameEngine handlers Membership-derived current actor/turn; pair preflight requires projected owned units to be co-located. The worker revalidates distinct IDs, ownership, co-location, one civilian plus one military unit, non-air types, bounds, reachability, entry legality, movement, terrain, and occupancy before moving both in one proposal; no client path, cost, compatibility result, or outcome is trusted Projection v58 retains owner-only movement routes and their optional companion ID plus sorted, distinct exact-move, multi-turn, and swap destinations for the authenticated current actor. Paired exact destinations are the canonical intersection for both units. Foreign order metadata and all foreign/out-of-turn action choices are absent The production projection-only world and opened-v3 controls consume cached exact destinations and fail closed when unavailable. Exact and multi-turn moves send only stable unit IDs and a destination; snapshot reload reconstructs transient shared-engine escort state only inside the worker. Local, hotseat, and legacy behavior is unchanged Complete for inventoried movement, durable escort routes, cancellation, and swaps Unit melee/ranged/city combat AttackWithUnit(unitId, targetX, targetY), BombardWithCity(cityId, targetX, targetY), LaunchNuclearStrike(unitId, targetX, targetY), and AirSweep(unitId, targetX, targetY) Focused Kotlin executors delegate to existing Battle, BattleDamage, Nuke, TargetHelper, and AirInterception engines Membership-derived actor/current turn; canonical ownership, capability, attacks/movement, setup, visibility/exploration, range/path/line of sight, war state, target/interceptor selection, blast victims, and deterministic RNG; clients claim no defender, path, strength, modifier, damage, victims, random values, or outcomes Projection v45 publishes sorted bounded visible attack/attack-from and bombard targets with canonical base/effective strengths, modifier summaries, health ranges, and closed capture outcomes. Nuclear candidates add only the own weapon's blast radius and a closed hidden-until-commit disclosure; air-sweep candidates add only own attacker strength/modifiers/health and the same closed interceptor disclosure. Candidate membership and metadata are invariant when hidden blast victims or interceptors change; accepted commands revalidate and reconcile every canonical result Opened-v3 right-click, highlighting, preflight, confirmation, and submission consume only cached projected choices and previews. The confirmation panel performs no local combat calculation and explicitly explains delayed nuclear/interceptor disclosure. Local, hotseat, legacy multiplayer, and server AI retain shared engine paths Complete Unit special actions DisbandUnit, FoundCity, ParadropUnit, UseReligiousUnit, closed UseGreatPersonUnit, GiftUnit, AddUnitToCapitalProject, opaque CreateInstantImprovement, TransformUnit, and TriggerUnitUnique are implemented; the airlift audit found rebasing already uses authoritative movement Existing shared unit actions and UnitActionsFromUniques callbacks through focused authoritative executors; Rust contains no rules engine Membership-derived current actor/turn and owned unit; projection-bound closed or opaque action identity; the worker re-derives targets, tiles, improvements, costs, resources, movement, conditionals, RNG, consumption, placement, capital/project identity, and effects Projection v57 exposes exact disband/pillage/found capability and sorted visible paradrop destinations alongside applicable religious, great-person, gift, capital-project, instant-improvement, transform, and trigger actions only for owned current-turn units; canonical effects reconcile after commit Both legacy-shaped opened-v3 controls and the disposable projection-only world submit through the authenticated session before local mutation. The projection-only controller rejects invented capability and coordinates before transport; local, hotseat, saves, legacy multiplayer, and server-owned AI retain shared Kotlin behavior Complete for the inventoried direct unit special-action surface Unit automation, orders, and postures SetUnitExploration(unitId, enabled) and SetUnitAutomation(unitId, enabled) implement exploration and generic automation start/stop; closed-enum SetUnitPosture(unitId, posture) implements Sleep, Sleep Until Healed, Fortify, Fortify Until Healed, Guard, and siege Setup; SetTileImprovementOrder handles same-tile worker construction/cancellation/repair; nullable-destination SetRoadConnectionOrder starts and cancels road automation Shared UnitAutomation, RoadToAutomation, posture/setup methods, tile improvement queues, durable paired movement orders, and existing canonical action semantics through focused modules and HeadlessGameEngine; pending automated unit actions execute in the private worker immediately before authoritative end-turn processing Membership-derived current actor/turn; own-unit preflight; canonical ownership, movement, escort compatibility, siege unique/embarkation/setup state, builder uniques, road technology, explored/passable/buildable destination, server-derived path, healing, fortification, improvement legality, repair state, and Guard validation; arbitrary action strings and client paths are impossible Projection v58 retains owner-only automation/exploration/order state and advertises exact worker-derived posture, improvement/repair/cancellation, and road-destination choices. Visible foreign and out-of-turn units receive false/empty/null private controls; Rust rejects reordered, duplicate, malformed, foreign, and out-of-turn choices The projection-only world renders exact exploration/automation flips, movement cancellation, promotions, swaps, postures, multi-turn destinations, improvement orders, and road start/cancellation. API v3 deliberately does not expose legacy whole-turn autoplay because that implementation runs client AI through WorldScreen; all real AI and pending unit automation run in the private worker. Local, hotseat, and legacy retain their existing autoplay controls Complete for the retained authoritative order surface Promotions, upgrades, and unit names Bounded UpgradeUnits; bounded PromoteUnit with server-derived optional city-default capture; SetCityUnitPromotionPreference(cityId, baseUnitName, enabled); nullable RenameUnit Shared upgrade, UnitPromotions.addPromotion, city saved-promotion application, and MapUnit.instanceName Membership-derived current actor/turn and stable owned IDs. Upgrade and promotion legality is canonical. Saving defaults requires the promoted unit to occupy an owned non-puppet city and clones its canonical promotion state. Preference toggles require an existing server-saved entry and accept no promotion/XP payload. Rename accepts null or 1-100 printable characters Projection v57 adds sorted, affordable, exact per-unit upgrade targets with canonical gold cost plus turn-scoped rename capability to the existing owner-only promotion/XP/name data. Foreign and out-of-turn projections expose none of these action choices The disposable projection-only world now renders promotions, each exact upgrade target/cost, and bounded rename input through the same authenticated command bus. Rust validates bounds, ordering, uniqueness, cancellation coherence, explored coordinates, and absence from foreign/out-of-turn units The production projection-only world and opened-v3 controls render exact worker choices and submit typed intents without local canonical mutation.
